Description: The system shall capture Ethernet packets on the Raspberry Pi interface at a minimum rate of 100 packets per second
Verification_Criteria: System successfully captures 100+ packets/second in test environment for 60 seconds continuous operation
Rationale: Minimum throughput needed for real-time detection of typical network attacks

Description: The system shall parse captured packets and extract source IP, destination IP, source port, destination port, protocol, packet length, and TCP flags
Verification_Criteria: All specified fields extracted correctly for 100 test packets with 100% accuracy
Rationale: Required packet metadata for ML feature engineering

Description: The system shall store captured packet data in PCAP format for offline analysis
Verification_Criteria: Generated PCAP files can be opened in Wireshark and contain all captured packets
Rationale: Enable post-analysis and debugging of detection results

Description: The system shall continue capturing packets even when storage is >80% full by implementing circular buffer mechanism
Verification_Criteria: System operates continuously for 24 hours with limited storage without crashes
Rationale: Prevent system failure due to storage limitations

Description: The system shall detect port scanning attacks with minimum 90% accuracy and maximum 5% false positive rate
Verification_Criteria: Detection accuracy ≥90% and false positive rate ≤5% on validation dataset of 1000 samples
Rationale: Industry standard for IDS performance

Description: The system shall detect DoS (Denial of Service) attacks with minimum 90% accuracy and maximum 5% false positive rate
Verification_Criteria: Detection accuracy ≥90% and false positive rate ≤5% on validation dataset of 1000 samples
Rationale: Critical attack type for network security

Description: The system shall detect data exfiltration attempts with minimum 85% accuracy
Verification_Criteria: Detection accuracy ≥85% on validation dataset of 500 samples
Rationale: Data exfiltration patterns are more subtle, 85% accuracy is acceptable

Description: The system shall extract network flow features including packet count, byte count, average packet size, inter-arrival time statistics, and protocol distribution within configurable time windows
Verification_Criteria: All specified features extracted correctly and values match manual calculation for 10 sample flows
Rationale: Essential features for ML-based attack detection

Description: The system shall process network traffic and generate attack alerts with maximum latency of 100ms from packet arrival to alert generation
Verification_Criteria: 95% of alerts generated within 100ms measured over 1000 detections
Rationale: Real-time detection requirement for effective threat response

Description: The system shall support training and updating ML models without system restart
Verification_Criteria: Successfully load new model and detect attacks without service interruption
Rationale: Enable model improvements without downtime

Description: The STM32 gateway shall detect malformed Ethernet packets (invalid length, corrupted headers, invalid checksums) with minimum 85% accuracy
Verification_Criteria: Detection accuracy ≥85% on test set of 500 malformed packets
Rationale: Fuzzing detection at edge provides first line of defense

Description: The TinyML model on STM32 shall have maximum size of 100KB including weights and architecture
Verification_Criteria: Compiled model binary size ≤100KB verified by checking file size
Rationale: STM32H755 flash memory constraint

Description: The STM32 shall perform fuzzing detection inference with maximum latency of 10ms per packet
Verification_Criteria: 95% of inferences complete within 10ms measured over 1000 packets
Rationale: Real-time processing requirement for gateway operation

Description: The STM32 TinyML model shall use maximum 50KB RAM during inference
Verification_Criteria: Peak RAM usage ≤50KB measured during inference execution
Rationale: STM32H755 has 1MB RAM, leave headroom for other functions

Description: The system shall simulate port scanning attacks targeting configurable port ranges at configurable rates (1-1000 ports/second)
Verification_Criteria: Generated traffic matches expected port scan pattern verified by packet analysis
Rationale: Required for testing detection capabilities

Description: The system shall simulate DoS attacks by generating high-rate traffic (up to 1000 packets/second) to target IP addresses
Verification_Criteria: Traffic rate measured at receiver matches configured rate ±5%
Rationale: Test system resilience to high traffic loads

Description: The system shall simulate fuzzing attacks by generating packets with randomized fields (invalid lengths, corrupted headers, random payloads)
Verification_Criteria: Generated packets contain expected malformations verified by manual inspection of 10 sample packets
Rationale: Test fuzzing detection capability of STM32

Description: The system shall simulate data exfiltration by generating sustained high-volume upload traffic to external IP addresses
Verification_Criteria: Traffic pattern matches expected exfiltration signature verified by IDS detection
Rationale: Test data exfiltration detection

Description: The attack simulator shall log all generated attack parameters (type, target, duration, rate) for test traceability
Verification_Criteria: Log file contains all required parameters for 10 simulated attacks
Rationale: Enable reproducible testing and debugging

Description: The Raspberry Pi and STM32 shall communicate via Ethernet using TCP/IP protocol with reliable delivery
Verification_Criteria: 100 consecutive messages exchanged without packet loss
Rationale: Reliable communication essential for system operation

Description: The STM32 shall report fuzzing detection alerts to Raspberry Pi within 50ms of detection
Verification_Criteria: 95% of alerts delivered within 50ms measured over 100 detections
Rationale: Timely alert delivery for coordinated threat response

Description: The system shall implement automatic reconnection if Ethernet connection is lost, with maximum 5 retry attempts
Verification_Criteria: System successfully reconnects after simulated cable disconnect within 10 seconds
Rationale: System resilience to network interruptions

Description: The system shall use static IP addressing for Pi (192.168.10.1) and STM32 (192.168.10.2) for predictable network configuration
Verification_Criteria: Both devices configured with specified IP addresses verified by ping test
Rationale: Simplify setup and avoid DHCP dependency

Description: The system shall include automated unit tests with minimum 80% code coverage for Python modules
Verification_Criteria: Coverage report shows ≥80% line coverage for all Python modules
Rationale: Industry best practice for code quality

Description: The CI/CD pipeline shall execute all tests and static analysis on every commit to main branch
Verification_Criteria: GitHub Actions workflow executes and completes for test commit
Rationale: Ensure code quality and prevent regressions

Description: The system shall run static code analysis (Pylint, Flake8) and fail builds with code quality score below 8.0/10
Verification_Criteria: Pipeline rejects code with quality score <8.0 demonstrated with intentionally poor code
Rationale: Maintain consistent code quality

Description: The Raspberry Pi shall connect to WiFi network and maintain stable connection with automatic reconnection on failure
Verification_Criteria: WiFi connection maintained for 24 hours with <1 minute total downtime
Rationale: Enable cloud data upload and remote monitoring

Description: The system shall upload attack detection alerts to cloud endpoint within 5 seconds of detection
Verification_Criteria: 90% of alerts uploaded within 5 seconds measured over 100 detections
Rationale: Timely cloud notification for remote monitoring

Description: The system shall buffer alerts locally when cloud connection is unavailable and upload when connection is restored
Verification_Criteria: Alerts buffered during 5-minute disconnection successfully uploaded after reconnection
Rationale: Ensure no alert loss during network outages

Description: The system shall provide real-time dashboard displaying current system status, alert count, and detection statistics
Verification_Criteria: Dashboard displays and updates within 5 seconds of system state change
Rationale: User visibility into system operation

Description: The system shall send email notifications for critical alerts (detected attacks) within 1 minute of detection
Verification_Criteria: Email received within 1 minute for 10 test alerts
Rationale: Remote notification capability

Description: The STM32 firmware shall implement Classic AUTOSAR architecture with BSW, RTE, and ASW layers
Verification_Criteria: Code structure follows AUTOSAR layering verified by architecture review
Rationale: Demonstrate automotive software architecture expertise

Description: The Raspberry Pi shall implement Adaptive AUTOSAR service-oriented architecture with ara::com communication
Verification_Criteria: Services communicate via ara::com demonstrated with test service calls
Rationale: Showcase next-generation automotive architecture

Description: The system shall support over-the-air firmware updates for both Raspberry Pi and STM32 with cryptographic signature verification
Verification_Criteria: Successfully update firmware and reject unsigned/tampered updates
Rationale: Demonstrate secure update capability

Description: The system shall implement A/B partition scheme for Raspberry Pi allowing rollback to previous firmware on update failure
Verification_Criteria: System successfully rolls back after simulated update failure
Rationale: Prevent bricking from failed updates

Description: The Raspberry Pi shall update STM32 firmware via Ethernet using secure bootloader protocol
Verification_Criteria: STM32 firmware successfully updated from Pi with integrity verification
Rationale: Centralized update management from Pi

Description: The STM32 shall implement secure boot chain verifying bootloader and application signatures before execution
Verification_Criteria: System refuses to boot with tampered/unsigned firmware
Rationale: Establish root of trust

Description: The system shall use hardware security module (TPM/ATECC608) for cryptographic key storage with keys never exposed in software
Verification_Criteria: Private keys used for signing but not readable from software demonstrated by test
Rationale: Protect cryptographic material

Description: All Ethernet communication between Pi and STM32 shall be encrypted using TLS 1.3
Verification_Criteria: Network traffic analysis shows encrypted payloads, decryption fails without proper keys
Rationale: Protect inter-device communication

Description: The system shall implement anti-tampering detection and wipe cryptographic keys if hardware tampering is detected
Verification_Criteria: Keys erased after simulated tampering event (voltage glitch, debug probe)
Rationale: Protect against physical attacks

Description: The system shall implement a watchdog mechanism where STM32 monitors Raspberry Pi health and initiates reset if Pi becomes unresponsive
Verification_Criteria: STM32 successfully detects missing heartbeat and resets Pi within timeout period
Rationale: Ensure system reliability and automatic recovery from Pi software failures

Description: The Raspberry Pi shall send heartbeat messages to STM32 at minimum interval of 2 seconds during normal operation
Verification_Criteria: Heartbeat messages sent every 2 seconds with <100ms jitter measured over 1000 samples
Rationale: Provide regular health status to watchdog for supervision

Description: The STM32 watchdog shall debounce heartbeat timeout by requiring 3 consecutive missed heartbeats before initiating reset action
Verification_Criteria: Reset triggered only after 6 seconds (3 x 2s intervals) of missing heartbeats, not on single missed heartbeat
Rationale: Avoid false positive resets due to temporary network glitches or processing delays

Description: The STM32 shall reset Raspberry Pi by controlling Pi's RUN pin with minimum 1 second assertion time
Verification_Criteria: Pi successfully reboots when RUN pin pulled low for 1 second, verified by boot sequence detection
Rationale: Provide hardware-level reset mechanism independent of Pi's software state

Description: The system shall log all watchdog reset events with timestamp and reason (heartbeat timeout, high CPU, high memory) to non-volatile storage
Verification_Criteria: Log file contains all reset events with timestamp, reason code, and pre-reset system state for last 10 resets
Rationale: Enable root cause analysis and system reliability monitoring

Description: The Raspberry Pi heartbeat message shall include system health metrics (CPU usage, memory usage, detection status)
Verification_Criteria: Heartbeat message contains valid CPU percentage (0-100), memory percentage (0-100), and detection active flag
Rationale: Enable proactive monitoring and intelligent reset decisions based on system health

Description: The STM32 watchdog shall optionally trigger reset if Raspberry Pi CPU usage remains above 95% for more than 30 seconds
Verification_Criteria: Reset triggered when CPU >95% sustained for 30 seconds, verified by artificial CPU load test
Rationale: Detect and recover from infinite loops or CPU-bound failure modes

Description: The watchdog mechanism shall be disabled automatically during Raspberry Pi firmware update operations
Verification_Criteria: Watchdog successfully disabled during FOTA update, Pi not reset during 5-minute update simulation
Rationale: Prevent interruption of critical firmware update process

Description: The system shall provide a RAG (Retrieval Augmented Generation) documentation assistant capable of answering natural language questions about project implementation
Verification_Criteria: RAG system successfully answers 20 test questions about code, architecture, and requirements with >90% accuracy
Rationale: Provide intelligent documentation access for project visitors and collaborators

Description: The RAG system shall index all project documentation including markdown files, source code, requirements CSV, and hardware datasheets
Verification_Criteria: Vector database contains embeddings for all docs, code files, requirements, and PDFs with successful retrieval test
Rationale: Enable comprehensive knowledge base covering all project artifacts

Description: The RAG system shall retrieve relevant code snippets with correct file paths and line numbers when queried about implementation details
Verification_Criteria: Code retrieval query returns correct file path, line numbers, and syntax-highlighted code snippet for 10 test queries
Rationale: Provide direct access to implementation details with proper source references

Description: The RAG system shall answer requirements traceability queries showing links between requirements, architecture, code, and tests
Verification_Criteria: Traceability query for any requirement returns correct architecture component, software requirements, and test cases
Rationale: Enable impact analysis and requirements coverage verification

Description: The RAG system shall provide responses within 5 seconds for 95% of queries under normal load conditions
Verification_Criteria: Response time <5 seconds for 95 of 100 test queries measured under simulated user load
Rationale: Ensure responsive user experience for documentation queries

Description: The RAG system shall be accessible via web interface with conversational chat UI supporting conversation history
Verification_Criteria: Web interface loads successfully, accepts queries, maintains conversation context for 10+ exchanges
Rationale: Provide user-friendly interface for project documentation access

Description: The RAG system shall cite source documents for all responses with clickable links to original content
Verification_Criteria: Every response includes source citations with working GitHub links to referenced documents/code
Rationale: Enable verification of information and exploration of source material

Description: The RAG system shall use Claude API for natural language generation with project-specific context
Verification_Criteria: RAG successfully integrates Claude API, generates coherent responses using retrieved context
Rationale: Leverage advanced LLM capabilities for high-quality natural language responses

Description: The RAG vector database shall use ChromaDB or equivalent with sentence-transformer embeddings for document retrieval
Verification_Criteria: Vector database configured with ChromaDB, embeddings generated using sentence-transformers model
Rationale: Use proven open-source tools for cost-effective RAG implementation

Description: The RAG system shall be deployed as publicly accessible web application with usage analytics
Verification_Criteria: RAG accessible via public URL, analytics show query count, response times, and user sessions
Rationale: Enable portfolio demonstration and track community engagement
